q.s: A 50-year-old man has taken omeprazole daily for 5 years. Serum gastrin is markedly elevated. Which mechanism explains this?
o: A gastrinoma caused by the PPI
Loss of acid-mediated inhibition of G cells
Reduced gastrin clearance by the kidney
e: Wrong. PPIs do not cause gastrinomas.
Correct. Gastrin release is suppressed by luminal pH <1.5; chronic acid suppression removes that brake.
Wrong. Somatostatin falls when acid is low.

q.s: Which cells secrete gastrin, and where are they located?
o: G cells; gastric antrum and duodenum

q.s: Vagal stimulation releases gastrin through which mediator?
e: Wrong. The vagus acts on G cells via GRP.

q.s: A patient with chronic atrophic gastritis from H. pylori has very high gastrin. Why?
o: Low acid production removes negative feedback on G cells

q.s: Which hormone, produced by the stomach, rises during fasting and stimulates appetite?
Which hormone is stimulated by acid and inhibits gastric acid, pepsinogen, pancreatic secretion, gallbladder contraction, insulin and glucagon?
Octreotide is used for all of the following EXCEPT:
e: Correct. Not an indication; achalasia relates to loss of NO and VIP neurons.

q.s: A fatty meal enters the duodenum. Which hormone causes gallbladder contraction and sphincter of Oddi relaxation?
e: Correct. Released by I cells in response to fatty acids and amino acids.

q.s: CCK increases pancreatic enzyme secretion mainly through which pathway?
o: Direct cAMP elevation in duct cells

q.s: What effect does CCK have on gastric emptying?
e: Correct. Gives more time for digestion in the duodenum.

q.s: Acid in the duodenum stimulates S cells to release which hormone?
e: Correct. Increases pancreatic HCO3− to neutralize acid so pancreatic enzymes can work.

q.s: Which hormone is responsible for greater insulin release after oral glucose than after IV glucose and also reduces gastric acid?
A patient with gastroparesis is given erythromycin to improve gastric emptying. Which receptor does it activate?
e: Correct. Motilin produces migrating motor complexes during fasting.

q.s: Migrating motor complexes during fasting are produced by which hormone?
A 50-year-old woman has profuse watery diarrhea (4 L/day), hypokalemia and achlorhydria. A pancreatic tumor is found. Which hormone does it secrete?
Loss of which neurotransmitter is implicated in the increased lower esophageal sphincter tone of achalasia?
e: Correct. NO relaxes smooth muscle including the LES.

q.s: Which factor inhibits gastrin release?
VIP has which effect on intestinal smooth muscle and secretion?
o: Relaxes smooth muscle and sphincters, increases water and electrolyte secretion

q.s: Which action is NOT attributed to gastrin?
After Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, patients report less hunger. Which hormonal change contributes?
A 64-year-old woman has megaloblastic anemia, glossitis and positive antiparietal cell antibodies. Loss of which secretory product causes her anemia?
e: Correct. Parietal cells secrete IF, needed for B12 absorption in the terminal ileum (pernicious anemia).

q.s: Gastrin increases acid secretion mainly by which mechanism?
o: Direct binding to parietal cells only
Stimulating ECL cells to release histamine, which acts on parietal cells

q.s: Which three stimuli increase parietal cell acid secretion?
Which substance inhibits gastric acid secretion?
e: Correct. Also somatostatin, GIP and secretin.

q.s: Pepsinogen is secreted by which cells and activated by what?
Where is bicarbonate that protects the gastric epithelium trapped?
o: In the mucus layer covering the epithelium

q.s: Which cells in the gastric body and fundus release histamine?
In the stomach, G cells are found mainly in which region?
Pancreatic juice at a high flow rate is rich in which anion?
e: Correct. Low flow → high Cl−, high flow → high HCO3−.

q.s: Which pancreatic enzymes are secreted in their active forms?
Trypsinogen is first converted to trypsin by which enzyme?
o: Enterokinase (enteropeptidase) on the duodenal brush border
e: Correct. Trypsin then activates other proenzymes and more trypsinogen (positive feedback).

q.s: A child with congenital enterokinase deficiency would have impaired digestion of which macronutrient?
e: Correct. Without enterokinase, trypsin is not activated, so proteases remain inactive.

q.s: Dipeptides and tripeptides are degraded where?
o: In the colon by bacteria only

q.s: Pancreatic secretion is overall what tonicity?
A patient on a histamine H2 blocker has reduced acid secretion. Which cell's receptor is blocked?
e: Correct. H2 receptors on parietal cells.

q.s: Which cells secrete pepsinogen in response to vagal stimulation?
Secretin acts mainly on which pancreatic cells?
Zymogen granules of pancreatic acinar cells contain which enzymes?
o: Trypsinogen, proelastase, chymotrypsinogen and procarboxypeptidases A and B

q.s: Somatostatin from gastric D cells is released in response to which stimulus?
Autoimmune destruction of which cells causes chronic gastritis with pernicious anemia?

rounds.t: Absorption, Peyer patches, bile, and bilirubin

q.s: Glucose and galactose enter enterocytes from the lumen through which transporter?
Which transporter moves all three monosaccharides from enterocytes into the blood?
A patient with chronic diarrhea has a D-xylose test: low blood and urine D-xylose after oral administration. What does this suggest?
o: Mucosal damage of the proximal small intestine (eg, celiac disease)
e: Correct. D-xylose is passively absorbed by healthy mucosa without needing pancreatic enzymes.
Wrong. D-xylose absorption is normal in pancreatic insufficiency.

q.s: Iron is absorbed mainly in which form and where?
o: Bound to intrinsic factor in the ileum

q.s: After resection of the terminal ileum for Crohn disease, a patient needs lifelong supplementation of which vitamin?
e: Wrong. Absorbed in the duodenum and jejunum.
Correct. Absorbed in the terminal ileum with intrinsic factor.

q.s: Folate is absorbed mainly where?
Thirty minutes after eating a sugary meal, a patient who had a gastrectomy has abdominal cramps, diarrhea, flushing and palpitations. Diagnosis?
e: Correct. Hyperosmolar food moves rapidly into the small intestine after gastric surgery.

q.s: Which specialized cells overlying Peyer patches sample luminal antigens?
B cells stimulated in Peyer patch germinal centers become plasma cells secreting which antibody?
e: Wrong. Not the main gut antibody.
Wrong. Not the main gut antibody.
Correct. Transported across the epithelium with secretory component.

q.s: Which enzyme catalyzes the rate-limiting step of bile acid synthesis?
A patient with ileal Crohn disease develops calcium oxalate kidney stones. Why?
o: Fat malabsorption lets calcium bind fat instead of oxalate, so more free oxalate is absorbed

q.s: Bile acids are conjugated to which molecules to become water soluble?
Which is the body's primary means of eliminating cholesterol?
Heme is converted to biliverdin by which enzyme?
Which form of bilirubin is water soluble and can appear in urine?
Gut bacteria convert conjugated bilirubin into which compound?
e: Correct. 80% excreted in feces as stercobilin; some reabsorbed and excreted in urine as urobilin.

q.s: The brown color of stool comes from which pigment?
Which enzyme conjugates bilirubin in the liver?
Fructose crosses the apical membrane of enterocytes by:
Bile salts that are not reabsorbed in the distal ileum (as after ileal resection) reach the colon and cause:
